speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. Please describe your neck and arm pain in detail: when did it start, is it constant or intermittent, and does it radiate in a specific pattern down your arm? Additionally, have you noticed any specific areas of muscle weakness or numbness?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of burning pain in his neck and arms, accompanying paresthesias in his hands. Over the past 3 months, he has experienced increasing weakness in both hands. He has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and hypertension. He was involved in a motor vehicle accident 3 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Cervical Spondylotic Myelopathy with Radiculopathy.

The patient's 1-year history of burning pain, paresthesias, and progressive bilateral hand weakness, combined with his age and diabetes risk factors, is highly suggestive of cervical spinal cord compression. Given the bilateral nature of the symptoms and the progression over 3 months, this warrants immediate neuro-imaging. REQUEST IMAGES: Cervical_Spine_MRI.
